source: Hillstrom MineThatData e-mail analytics challenge dataset (.data/hillstrom.csv, 64,000 customers)
company_context: Mid-sized catalog/online merchandiser; customer file of 64,000 people who purchased within the last twelve months; customers segmented by dollars spent in the past year (history_segment), recency, channel, and urban/suburban/rural zip class.
control: No email is sent (holdout group).
treatment: Customers receive an email campaign featuring men's-merchandise merchandise.
prose: A catalog and online merchandiser ran an email test on customers who had purchased within the last twelve months. Customers were randomized to one of three groups: an email campaign featuring men's merchandise, an email campaign featuring women's merchandise, or no email at all. This case compares the men's-merchandise email campaign against the no-email holdout. Outcomes were tracked for two weeks following the campaign delivery. The primary metric is the website visit rate over the two-week window.

arm_a_tables.description: Baseline-only aggregates available before launch: customer-file segment mix (pre-treatment covariate) and baseline outcome rates by history segment from the no-contact holdout population (proxy for historical baseline). Contains no treatment-arm information and no treatment contrast.

arm_b_tables.description: Pilot-only per-arm aggregates for metric 'visit_rate': a 20% random subsample of the customer file (seed 20260701), drawn deterministically and independently of any outcome. Per-arm n and rate, overall and by history segment.

availability_notes: Honest post-pilot simulation: Arm B tables are aggregates from a deterministic 20% random pilot subsample (seed 20260701) of the customer file; the truth is computed on the FULL dataset, so the pilot is a genuine noisy preview, not a restatement of the truth. Arm A tables are baseline-only (segment mix + no-contact holdout baseline rates by segment) and encode no treatment contrast. The no-contact baseline is taken from the no-email arm as a proxy for historical baseline rates.

source: Cookie Cats A/B test (public dataset mirror); per-arm engagement-bin cross-tabs from e1_cookiecats_tables.json
company_context: Free-to-play mobile puzzle game (Cookie Cats, Tactile Games); roughly 90,000 new players in the test; monetization includes in-app purchases at forced progress gates.
control: The first forced progress gate is placed at level 30.
treatment: The first forced progress gate is placed at level 40.
prose: A free-to-play mobile puzzle game places forced progress gates at fixed levels; when a player reaches a gate they must wait for a timer or make an in-app purchase to continue playing. In the control condition the first gate appears at level 30. In the treatment condition the first gate appears at level 40. New players were randomly assigned to one gate placement when they installed the game. The primary metric is 1-day retention: whether the player opens the game again one day after installing.

arm_b_tables.description: Per-arm cross-tabs of users and retention rate by engagement bin (game rounds played in the first 14 days). NOTE: these are FULL-experiment aggregates, not a pilot subsample.

availability_notes: CIRCULARITY LIMITATION: the Arm B tables are FULL-experiment per-arm aggregates (the entire 90k-player test collapsed to engagement bins), NOT a pilot subsample - any Arm B call on this case is computed from the same data that defines the truth. No baseline-only tables are available, so Arm A tables are null (strict pre-launch arm must abstain or work from prose alone). Same underlying experiment as cur_01 in the curated stratum.

source: Duolingo engineering/blog (via PORTFOLIO_CASES_V3.json)
company_context: Consumer language-learning app with a daily-streak habit mechanic (consecutive days of practice).
control: Missing a day of practice ends the user's streak.
treatment: An equippable 'Weekend Amulet' item keeps the streak active through one skipped weekend day.
prose: A language-learning app tracks a daily streak: the number of consecutive days a user has practiced. In the control condition, missing a day of practice ends the streak. In the treatment condition, users can equip an item called the Weekend Amulet that keeps the streak active through one skipped weekend day. Users were randomly assigned to one condition. The primary metric is the week-later return rate: whether the user returns to the app a week later.
availability_notes: Published narrative case; no per-arm aggregate tables available (arm tables null).
